Likelihood-ratio test between nested DAMOCLES fits

Source: R/damocles_regimes.R
damocles_lrt.Rd

damocles_lrt() compares two fits of damocles_fit() to the same communities, where null is a special case of alternative: constant rates against rates that change among regimes or with an edge_covariate (where beta = 0 gives the constant model), rates shared by all communities against separate rates, or sympatry = 0 against an estimated sympatry. Twice the difference of the total log-likelihoods is compared with a chi-squared distribution with as many degrees of freedom as extra parameters.

Usage

damocles_lrt(null, alternative)

Arguments

null, alternative

Fits of class mc_damocles_fit to the same communities.

Value

A data frame with one row per model: number of free parameters, total log-likelihood, AIC, and, for the alternative, the statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value.

Details

The function counts parameters but cannot check that the models are nested; that is up to the user. When the null value lies on the boundary of the parameter space, as sympatry = 0 or a rate of zero in one regime, the chi-squared p-value is conservative. The test answers whether the partition or covariate improves the fit to the local presences; with partitions or covariates estimated from the same tree by methods of diversification, a significant result is an association between those rates and the local dynamics, not evidence of a mechanism.

See also

damocles_fit(), clade_regimes().

Other dynamic null model: clade_regimes(), confint.mc_damocles_fit(), damocles_loglik(), damocles_test(), simulate_damocles()

Examples

set.seed(5)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(40)
reg <- clade_regimes(tr, list(A = ape::extract.clade(tr, ape::Ntip(tr) + 2)$tip.label))
comm <- simulate_damocles(tr, gamma = 1, mu = 1, n = 5)
constant <- damocles_fit(comm, tr, shared = TRUE)
by_clade <- damocles_fit(comm, tr, shared = TRUE, regimes = reg, vary = "gamma")
damocles_lrt(constant, by_clade)
#>             n_par    loglik      AIC    statistic df   p_value
#> null            2 -91.68836 187.3767           NA NA        NA
#> alternative     3 -91.68833 189.3767 6.611732e-05  1 0.9935123
